name: Multi-Agent Cross-Device Encrypted Collaboration (Email + Task Sealing)
description: Functional skill for coordinating multi-agent cross-device encrypted collaboration using MGC 1.6.0 chain mode. Split a workflow by data domain into N sealed sub-packages — each execution agent receives only the scripts authorized for its domain. Data and credentials never leave local storage; only task cards, scripts, and result summaries flow across devices. Default transport is email; task payloads travel as sealed sub-packages.
author: MirginCipher Team

changes: Initial release based on MGC 1.6.0 chain mode
Three reference roles: orchestrator agent / internal execution agent / external execution agent, split by data domain
Eight-stage collaboration protocol: prepare → author → store → seal → dispatch → execute → return → aggregate
Hard constraints: data and credentials never ship inside sub-packages; workflow directory must be flat; targets files must exactly match diff_3
Default transport: email with Subject keyword chain:<task_id> and sha256 in body; also supports A2A / HTTPS / shared folder
distribution_index.json drives automated dispatch; node fingerprint ledger matches each sub-package to recipient
UNSEAL_FAILED error code: import success does NOT guarantee unsealing — node_pub mismatch surfaces only at run time
ext01 portability reminder (python vs python3) and --output parent-directory pre-create requirement
script-wrapped encryption pattern: task prompts and result summaries sealed inside .py files alongside execution scripts
Five role_prompts templates: orchestrator task card / dispatch instructions / executor task card / result return / orchestrator return receipt
examples: role_prompts.md, use_credential.py (local MGC credential access), task_flow.md (fill-in template)
Targets specs contain .py only; data files and credentials stay in each executor's local MGC
Boundary with single-device soft-isolation skill (task_chain_meta_skill) clearly defined
